predecessors.name: French Africa
predecessors.text: the four colonies Senegal, French Sudan, French Guinea and Ivory Coast, already French land in Cliopatria's French Africa shape of 1895

successors.name: Republic of Senegal
successors.text: Senegal, an autonomous republic within the French Community after the 1958 referendum

successors.name: Mali
successors.text: French Sudan (the Sudanese Republic), with Senegal the Mali Federation of 1959-60

successors.name: Guinea
successors.text: 'Guinea voted overwhelmingly for independence' in the 1958 referendum

ledger.x: 1895: the French are still fighting Samory Ture's Wassoulou empire.
1895 (27 October): French West Africa is created at Saint-Louis as a union of Senegal, French Sudan, French Guinea and Ivory Coast.
1896: the French claim the Mossi country.
1898 (29 September): Samory is captured and his empire ends.
1898 (29 September): fighting with Samory ends with his capture at Guelemou by Captain Gouraud.
1901: Ouagadougou falls and the Mossi country is French.
1901: the Mossi resistance ends with the capture of Ouagadougou.
1902: the governor-general moves from Saint-Louis to Dakar.
1904: Mauritania becomes part of French West Africa.
1922: Niger becomes a French colony within the West African system.
1934: the League of Nations mandate of French Togoland is attached to Dahomey.
1937: the Togoland attachment to Dahomey ends.

wars.name: French conquest of the Wassoulou Empire
wars.outcome: French victory: Samory captured by Gouraud at Guelemou on 29 September 1898 and 'Samoridugu ceased to exist'.

wars.name: French conquest of the Mossi country

certainty.note: Inland and Saharan frontiers (Mauritania, Niger, French Sudan north) are administrative and approximate; frontiers against Gambia, the Gold Coast and Nigeria were fixed by treaties that no page opened gives.
